title: Greek Chicken Gyro Wraps
description: Lemon-and-oregano marinated chicken, a quick grated-cucumber tzatziki, and a build-your-own bar so everyone rolls their own.

items: Oven chips (they go inside the wrap)

steps: Marinate first, then prep everything else while it sits. Mix the garlic, olive oil, lemon, oregano, paprika and salt. Cut the thighs into strips — more surface area means the 20 minutes does more work — then coat and set aside.
Make the tzatziki. Grate the cucumber, wring the water out in a tea towel, then stir it into the yoghurt with the garlic and a pinch of salt. Into the fridge.
Prep the fillings. Slice the tomato and onion, shred the lettuce, grate cheese if using. Lay it all out bar-style.
Cook hot and fast. Get the pan properly hot. The strips need just 3–4 minutes, tossing, until charred at the edges and no pink inside. Don't crowd the pan.
Warm the wraps for a few seconds in the dry pan so they fold without cracking.
Lift the short marinade — a squeeze of fresh lemon and a pinch of oregano over the cooked chicken makes up for the quick soak.

Build your own: warm wrap laid flat, a smear of tzatziki down the middle (not the edges, or it squeezes out), chicken strips down the centre, chips if you're going full gyro, then salad and a little onion. Fold one end up first, then roll tight and wrap the base so nothing drops out.
notes: Kids' jobs: grating and wringing the cucumber, mixing the tzatziki, and running the build-your-own line — same appeal as a taco bar. No time to pre-marinate? Cutting the chicken into strips lets 20 minutes do real work, and with strips you can skip resting the meat too. One 500 g tub of Greek yoghurt covers the tzatziki here and a two-ingredient naan another night.

items.name: Lemons
items.hint: 1 juiced for the marinade, wedges to serve

items.name: Red onion
items.hint: recipe uses ¼, but they don't sell quarters

items.name: Souvlaki bread or wraps
items.hint: the medium one — not the thin pocket pita

items.name: Greek yoghurt, thick
items.hint: need 1 cup — tub also covers a naan another night

items.name: Oven chips
items.hint: if going full gyro — chips go inside the wrap

title: Fettuccine Alfredo
description: Silky, restaurant-style alfredo. The sauce comes together in about the time the pasta cooks.
ingredients: 400 g fettuccine (dried is fine) — use ~330 g if scaling the sauce down
85 g unsalted butter (about ⅓ of a 250 g block)
200–240 ml cream (thickened or pure cream is easiest)
100 g Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated — plus extra for serving
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Optional: 2 garlic cloves (minced), a pinch of nutmeg
steps: Boil the pasta. Big pot of well-salted water. Cook the fettuccine until just shy of al dente (~12 min is normal). Before draining, scoop out a mug of the starchy pasta water.
Melt the butter in a wide pan on low heat. (Add the garlic now if using — about 1 minute, don't let it brown.)
Pour the cream into the melted butter and heat gently until steaming, not boiling.
Cheese goes in off the heat. Pull the pan off the burner and let it stop bubbling, then add the parmesan a handful at a time, whisking each lot in smoothly before the next.

Drain the pasta (don't rinse) and return it to its pot, then pour the sauce over it. Toss hard, splashing in pasta water bit by bit until the sauce turns silky and coats every strand. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately on warm plates with extra parmesan grated over the top. Alfredo stiffens as it sits, so don't let it wait.
notes: The rules that matter most: keep the heat low (heat is what breaks the sauce); add the cheese off the heat (too hot turns it grainy and stringy); pasta water is your fix — if it ever looks tight, oily or split, a splash plus hard tossing pulls it back together; and use a real block of parmesan grated yourself, since pre-shredded has anti-caking starch that won't melt cleanly. To level up later, drop the cream entirely and make the Roman version: just butter, parmesan and pasta water emulsified together.

items.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano
items.hint: a real block to grate — not pre-shredded

title: Lemonade
description: A fresh 1-litre jug. The sugar goes into hot water first so it fully dissolves — never grainy.
steps: Mix the boiling water with the sugar, stirring until it fully dissolves.
Stir in the lemon juice.
Add the cold water and mix — that brings it to 1 litre.
Chill in the fridge, then serve over ice.
notes: Makes about 1 litre. Start at 6 tbsp sugar and taste — lemons vary, so add more if it's too sharp.

title: Crispy Chicken With Lime Butter
description: Thighs slow-seared almost entirely skin-side down, with a lime-and-maple pan sauce emulsified with cold butter. Shatteringly crisp skin, no thermometer needed.
ingredients: 4 large bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 900 g)
1 1/2 tsp salt, plus more to season the sauce
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus wedges to serve
3 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cut into pats
Parsley, coriander, basil or mint leaves, to serve (optional)
steps: Pat the thighs thoroughly dry, season all over with the salt and pepper, and leave at room temperature 10–30 minutes. Blot dry again before cooking — dry skin is the whole game.

Heat a large heavy skillet (cast iron is ideal) over medium. Add the oil and swirl to coat. Lay the chicken in skin-side down and leave it completely alone for 20–25 minutes, dropping to medium-low if it colours too fast. When the steady sputtering fades, the moisture has driven off and the skin is set.

Add the garlic, flip the chicken, and cook another 5 minutes until lightly browned underneath and cooked through. Move to a plate skin-side up. Pour off the rendered fat, keeping about 3 tbsp in the pan.
Add the stock, lime juice and maple syrup and season. Bring to a simmer over high, then pull back to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half — about 3 minutes.

Add the cold butter and keep at a bare simmer, stirring constantly, until incorporated. The sauce thickens and turns glossy. Too hot and it splits, so ease off the heat if needed. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve with lime wedges and herbs, dressed with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt. Something starchy alongside catches the sauce.

variations.title: No stock
variations.body: Swap the 1/2 cup stock for 1/4 cup water. Less depth, but the butter carries it.

notes: NYT Cooking, Eric Kim — from their Top 50 of 2025. Don't touch the chicken during the long sear — moving it tears the skin before it releases. If the sauce breaks, pull the pan off the heat and whisk in another cold pat of butter or a splash of stock. Standard-size thighs rather than large ones want closer to 18 minutes on the skin side. Dark meat tastes best around 82°C, above the 74°C safety minimum, because the connective tissue needs the extra time.

items.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in skin-on
items.hint: bone-in and skin-on — fillets will not work here

items.name: Fresh herbs
items.hint: optional — parsley, coriander, basil or mint

items.name: Maple syrup
items.hint: need 2 tsp — real maple, not pancake syrup

title: Chicken Souvlaki Bowl
description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, air-fried oregano potatoes, chopped Greek salad and tzatziki, built as four bowls. Everything but the marinade comes together while the potatoes cook.

items: 800 g chicken breast, cut into chunks

steps: Marinate the chicken first. Combine the chicken with the yoghurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper. Mix well and leave at least 30 minutes. Thread onto skewers if you have them.

Dice the potatoes small, then toss with the oregano, garlic powder, paprika, salt, pepper and a few sprays of olive oil. Air fry at 200°C / 400°F for 20 minutes, shaking halfway, then finish with the lemon juice.
Air fry the chicken at 200°C / 400°F for about 12 minutes, until cooked through and lightly charred at the edges.
Chop the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and parsley into a bowl. Add the lemon juice and a small pinch of salt and mix.
Grate the cucumber for the tzatziki and wring out as much water as you can in a clean tea towel. Stir it into the yoghurt with the garlic, lemon juice, dill if using, salt and pepper until smooth.
Divide the potatoes, chicken, salad and tzatziki between four bowls.
notes: Buy 2 cucumbers — the salad takes a large one diced and the tzatziki another half, grated. 1200 g of diced potato will not fit one air fryer basket in a single layer; do it in two batches or they steam instead of crisping, and hold the first batch warm in the oven. The yoghurt in the marinade tenderises, so it works fine at 30 minutes but is better left a few hours. Components keep separately in the fridge for 3–4 days, so it portions well ahead; keep the tzatziki off the potatoes until serving. The original omits dill from the ingredient list but calls for it in the tzatziki step.

items.name: Cucumbers
items.hint: 1 large diced for the salad, ½ grated for the tzatziki

items.name: 0% Greek yoghurt
items.hint: 2 cups all up — ½ marinade + 1½ tzatziki, nothing spare

title: Buttered Pasta
description: Pasta boiled in heavily salted water and tossed with unsalted butter until glossy. No sauce, four ingredients, ten minutes. Prawns or steak turn it into a full meal.
ingredients: 200 g dried pasta, any short shape
steps: Bring 3-4 L of water to a rolling boil. Add the salt - about a tablespoon, more than you would use if a sauce were going on. With no sauce, the water is the only seasoning the pasta gets.
Add the pasta and cook to the time on the packet. Before draining, scoop out half a mug of the cooking water and keep it.
Drain the pasta and return it to the hot, dry pot off the heat. Add the butter and toss until it has fully melted and coated every piece.
If it looks dry or the butter sits in a pool, add a splash of the reserved water and keep tossing. The starch in the water and the butter pull together into a light glaze.
Crack black pepper over and serve straight away.

variations.title: With prawns
variations.body: A 500 g bag of frozen cooked and peeled prawns (Coles sell these tail-off). Thaw under cold running water and pat dry. Melt a knob of butter in a frying pan over medium heat and toss the prawns for 2-3 minutes, just until heated through - they are already cooked, so any longer and they go rubbery. Tip the pan contents, butter and all, over the pasta.

variations.title: With steak
variations.body: One or two steaks from a Coles pack. Salt them and pan fry over high heat to your liking, then rest 5 minutes on a board. While resting, drop a knob of butter into the hot pan with a pinch of garlic powder or pepper and swirl until foaming. Slice the steak against the grain, put it over the pasta and pour the spiced butter and resting juices on top.

notes: Unsalted butter is the right call here - the pasta water already carries all the salt, and salted butter on top of that overshoots. Use the reserved pasta water freely; it is the difference between a glaze and butter sliding off. Both proteins cook in the time the pasta boils, so nothing needs to wait. Frozen cooked prawns are the lowest-effort protein of the two: no raw handling, no doneness to judge.

items.name: Unsalted butter
items.hint: 25-30 g for the pasta, plus a knob if doing prawns or steak

title: Apple Turnovers
description: Warm cinnamon apples wrapped in crispy puff pastry.
ingredients: Milk or 1 beaten egg for brushing (optional)
steps: Heat oven to 200°C, or 180°C fan-forced.
Peel apples if desired and cut into small cubes.
Melt a small knob of butter in a pan.
Add apples, cinnamon and 1 tsp sugar.
Add a small splash of water and cook for 5–8 minutes.
Keep the apples slightly firm. Taste and add another teaspoon of sugar only if needed.
Let the mixture cool slightly.
Cut puff pastry into squares and place a spoonful of filling in the centre.
Fold diagonally into triangles and press edges closed with a fork.
Cut a small slit in the top and optionally brush with milk or beaten egg.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until puffed and golden.
notes: Leftover cinnamon apples are great warmed up over waffles.

title: Butter Cookies
description: Simple, buttery and perfect for adding colours.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C, or 160°C fan-forced.
Mix softened butter and sugar until creamy.
Mix in vanilla.
Add flour and salt and mix until a soft dough forms.
For coloured cookies, divide the dough and knead a few drops of colouring into each portion.
Roll into small balls, place on a lined tray and flatten slightly.
Bake for 10–14 minutes, until the edges are just starting to turn golden.
Leave on the tray for 5 minutes before moving them to cool.
notes: Don't wait for the whole cookie to brown. Just-golden edges keep them tender and buttery.

title: Chocolate Pudding
description: Rich and chocolatey without being overly sweet.
steps: Put the cornflour, cocoa and sugar into a saucepan.
Add about ½ cup of cold milk and stir until completely smooth.
Pour in the remaining milk and stir.
Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously.
After about 5 minutes it should begin to bubble and thicken.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla and optional dark chocolate.
Pour into bowls. Eat warm, or refrigerate for about 2 hours.
notes: Not too sweet: start with 2 tbsp sugar. You can always increase it next time.
